rule: each dot may move <= 2 px onto the strongest smoothed magnetic-edge response in its window, subject to a 0.25 sigma gain gate and a 2.828 px spacing floor; count, mass and catalogue exclusion unchanged

model.hypothesis: If sharpness is what the kernel rewards, the vertical gradient should snap better than the horizontal one, because it localises a contact more tightly.
model.mechanism: The vertical derivative of a potential field is a shorter-wavelength enhancement of the same source edge; at a given flight-line spacing it discriminates neighbouring contacts that the horizontal gradient smears into one 2 px-wide maximum.
model.confounder: Short-wavelength enhancement amplifies interpolation noise between the 400 m GeoDAWN lines, so the 'peak' can be an artifact of the survey geometry rather than the geology.
model.falsifier: vg2 weaker than hg2 by more than 0.01 argues that the extra sharpening is noise; vg2 beating hg2 by >= 0.01 would say kernel-scale sharpness, not edge existence, is the binding constraint.
